title: 225. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Determining Parameter Ranges for Equation Solutions
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Parameter conditions for a linear equation with a unique solution
questions.learningObjective: Determine the condition on \(k\) for \(kx=3\) to have exactly one solution.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does the equation \(kx=3\) have exactly one solution?
questions.explanation: If \(k\ne 0\), dividing both sides by \(k\) gives the unique solution \(x=\frac{3}{k}\). If \(k=0\), the equation becomes \(0=3\), which is false and has no solution. Therefore exactly one solution occurs when \(k\ne 0\).
questions.hint: Consider whether the coefficient of \(x\) is zero or nonzero.

questions.concept: Parameter conditions for real solutions of \(x^2=m\)
questions.learningObjective: Determine the condition on \(m\) for \(x^2=m\) to have at least one real solution.
questions.question: For which values of \(m\) does the equation \(x^2=m\) have at least one real solution?
questions.explanation: For real \(x\), the square \(x^2\) is always nonnegative. If \(m>0\), there are two real solutions \(x=\pm\sqrt{m}\). If \(m=0\), there is exactly one real solution \(x=0\). If \(m<0\), there is no real solution. Therefore at least one real solution occurs when \(m\ge0\).
questions.hint: Recall that a square of a real number cannot be negative.

questions.concept: Parameter conditions for two distinct real roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(k\) for \(x^2+kx+1=0\) to have two distinct real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(x^2+kx+1=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation: The discriminant is \(\Delta=k^2-4(1)(1)=k^2-4\). For two distinct real roots, require \(\Delta>0\). Thus \(k^2-4>0\), so \(k^2>4\). This gives \(k<-2\) or \(k>2\).
questions.hint: Use the discriminant condition \(\Delta>0\) for two distinct real roots.

questions.concept: Parameter conditions for no real roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(k\) for \(x^2+kx+4=0\) to have no real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(x^2+kx+4=0\) have no real roots?
questions.explanation: The discriminant is \(\Delta=k^2-4(1)(4)=k^2-16\). For no real roots, require \(\Delta<0\). Thus \(k^2-16<0\), so \(k^2<16\). This gives \(-4<k<4\).
questions.hint: Use the discriminant condition \(\Delta<0\) for no real roots.

questions.concept: Parameter conditions for a rational equation with no solution
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(k\) for \(\frac{x}{x-1}=k\) to have no solution.
questions.question: For which value of \(k\) does the equation \(\frac{x}{x-1}=k\) have no solution?
questions.explanation: The domain excludes \(x=1\). If \(k=1\), the equation becomes \(\frac{x}{x-1}=1\). Multiplying by \(x-1\) gives \(x=x-1\), so \(0=-1\), which is impossible. Therefore the equation has no solution when \(k=1\). If \(k=0\), the solution \(x=0\) is valid.
questions.hint: Check the special value that makes the cleared equation contradictory.

questions.concept: Parameter conditions for a radical equation with a real solution
questions.learningObjective: Determine the condition on \(k\) for \(\sqrt{x}=k\) to have at least one real solution.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(\sqrt{x}=k\) have at least one real solution?
questions.explanation: The principal square root \(\sqrt{x}\) is defined for \(x\ge0\) and is nonnegative. If \(k>0\), then \(x=k^2\) gives a solution. If \(k=0\), then \(x=0\) gives \(\sqrt{0}=0\). If \(k<0\), no real square root can equal \(k\). Therefore at least one real solution occurs when \(k\ge0\).
questions.hint: Remember that a square root cannot equal a negative number.

questions.concept: Parameter conditions for an absolute value equation with exactly one solution
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(k\) for \(|x|=k\) to have exactly one solution.
questions.question: For which value of \(k\) does \(|x|=k\) have exactly one solution?
questions.explanation: If \(k>0\), then \(|x|=k\) gives \(x=k\) or \(x=-k\), which are two distinct solutions. If \(k=0\), then \(|x|=0\), so \(x=0\), giving exactly one solution. If \(k<0\), there is no solution. Therefore exactly one solution occurs when \(k=0\).
questions.hint: Consider how many values have a given distance from zero.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(k\) for \(x^2+(k-2)x+1=0\) to have real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(x^2+(k-2)x+1=0\) have real roots?
questions.explanation:
The discriminant is
\[
\Delta=(k-2)^2-4(1)(1)=(k-2)^2-4
\]
For real roots, require \(\Delta\ge0\). Thus \((k-2)^2\ge4\). This gives \(k-2\le-2\) or \(k-2\ge2\), so \(k\le0\) or \(k\ge4\).
questions.hint: Use the discriminant condition \(\Delta\ge0\) for real roots.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the values of \(k\) for \(x^2+kx+k+3=0\) to have equal roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(x^2+kx+k+3=0\) have equal roots?
questions.explanation:
Equal roots occur when the discriminant is zero. Compute the discriminant, then factor:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta &= k^2-4(1)(k+3)\\
&= k^2-4k-12\\
&= (k-6)(k+2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Setting \((k-6)(k+2)=0\) gives \(k=6\) or \(k=-2\).
questions.hint: Set the discriminant equal to zero and solve the resulting quadratic equation in \(k\).

questions.concept: Parameter conditions for two distinct negative roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the condition on \(k\) for \(x^2+(k+1)x+k=0\) to have two distinct negative roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(x^2+(k+1)x+k=0\) have two distinct negative roots?
questions.explanation:
Factor the quadratic:
\[
x^2+(k+1)x+k=(x+1)(x+k)
\]
The roots are \(x=-1\) and \(x=-k\). For both roots to be negative, we need \(-k<0\), so \(k>0\). For the roots to be distinct, we need \(-k\ne -1\), so \(k\ne 1\). Therefore the condition is \(k>0\) and \(k\ne 1\).
questions.hint: Factor the quadratic and then impose the conditions for both roots to be negative and distinct.
